candidate_title: Decision dependency tracing and change-impact analysis for Casbin
scenario_goal: Casbin's Enforcer answers enforce(subject, object, action) with a bare boolean. Security reviewers and operators cannot see which policy lines and role links produced that answer, and cannot tell whether editing one policy line would flip the decision for a given request. The task is to add decision tracing plus a change-impact query: enforce_traced returns the answer together with the exact rules and role links that were consulted and the subset that actually decided the outcome under the configured policy effect, and would_change answers whether applying a described policy mutation would alter the decision for one request. Success means the traced rules are exact for every supported effect type, domain and role-inheritance shape, and that would_change agrees with actually applying the mutation and re-enforcing, while plain enforce and all existing APIs keep their current behaviour.
actors: Application or gateway code calling enforce and needing an audit trail of the decision.
Security reviewer or auditor inspecting why a subject was allowed or denied.
Policy administrator evaluating the blast radius of a proposed policy edit before committing it.
The role manager serving role-inheritance queries for the same enforcer.
domain_objects: Policy lines (p rules) with an index, request key and values.
Role links (g rules) including domain-scoped links and multi-level inheritance.
Requests as (subject, domain, object, action) tuples.
Decision traces holding consulted rules, decisive rules and the effect outcome.
Policy mutations describing added or removed policy and role lines.
workflow: Caller requests a traced decision for one request tuple.
The enforcer resolves role inheritance for the subject within the request domain, then evaluates candidate policy lines.
Matching lines are collected in policy order and combined according to the model's policy effect.
The trace reports which lines matched, which of those actually fixed the outcome, and which effect branch terminated the decision.
Caller asks would_change for a described mutation; the enforcer decides whether the outcome for that request would differ after the mutation.
If the mutation is applied for real, a later enforce must agree with the earlier would_change answer.
state_and_lifecycle: Traces are values, snapshot-stable, and must not be invalidated by later policy edits.
Role link resolution is transitive: a link added two levels up changes the consulted set for a descendant subject.
Domain isolation: a role link or policy line scoped to one domain must never appear in another domain's trace.
A mutation that removes a line the trace marks decisive must flip the answer; removing a merely consulted line must not.
Added lines only change the answer when they outrank or override the existing outcome under the effect type.
The enforcer's live policy state stays authoritative; cached traces never feed back into enforce.
conflicts_failures_recovery: A request matches several lines that disagree; the effect type decides which one wins and the trace must name it.
A deny-override model where a single matched deny line must be reported as decisive even though allow lines also matched.
A priority model where the lowest priority number wins even though it appears later in the policy file.
An allow-and-deny model that terminates after the first decisive line, so later matching lines must be reported as consulted but not decisive.
Role inheritance cycles and duplicate role links must not cause infinite expansion or duplicated trace entries.
Requesting a trace for a request whose subject has no role links must still report subject-level policy lines.
would_change for a mutation that touches an unrelated domain or an unrelated object must answer no.
observable_outcomes: enforce_traced returns the same boolean that enforce would return for the same request.
Traces identify consulted rules by their stable policy index and values.
would_change agrees with apply-then-enforce for every mutation shape, including no-op mutations.
Traces for different domains never leak each other's lines.
Existing enforce, batch_enforce, role APIs and adapter behaviour are unchanged.
verifier_behaviors: Distinguish consulted rules from decisive rules under each effect type.
Distinguish a decisive removal from an irrelevant removal in would_change.
Check transitive and domain-scoped role resolution inside the consulted set.
Check that trace identity and ordering follow policy declaration order, not match order.
Check agreement between would_change and real apply plus enforce.
Check that traces survive later policy edits unchanged.
Check that role link cycles and duplicates do not corrupt the trace.
task_difficulties: Deciding what 'decisive' means per effect type instead of reporting every matched rule.
Resolving transitive role inheritance once and reusing it for both the decision and the trace without leaking across domains.
Making removal impact exact: a mutation can matter even when the removed line was not decisive, and can be irrelevant even when it was consulted.
Making addition impact exact under priority and override effects rather than assuming new lines always win.
Keeping the live decision path and the change-impact path from drifting apart so they cannot contradict.
Handling cycles, duplicate links and empty role sets without infinite expansion or duplicated entries.
